audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's final oath/defense: covenant with eyes, integrity scales, justice toward servants, poor, widow, orphan, refusal of wealth-idolatry, hospitality, transparency, land ethics, and closing of Job's words.

verses.restored: I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze upon a young woman?

familiar.text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

modern.text: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?

original.text: בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י וּמָ֥ה אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן עַל בְּתוּלָֽה

verses.restored: For what would be the portion of the Divine from above, or the inheritance of Shaddai from on high?

familiar.text: For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?

modern.text: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?

original.text: וּמֶ֤ה חֵ֣לֶק אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת שַׁ֝דַּ֗י מִמְּרֹמִֽים

verses.restored: Is not calamity for the unjust, and disaster for workers of harm?

familiar.text: Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?

modern.text: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity?

original.text: הֲלֹא אֵ֥יד לְעַוָּ֑ל וְ֝נֵ֗כֶר לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן

verses.restored: Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?

familiar.text: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?

modern.text: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?

original.text: הֲלֹא ה֭וּא יִרְאֶ֣ה דְרָכָ֑י וְֽכָל צְעָדַ֥י יִסְפּֽוֹר

verses.restored: If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit,

familiar.text: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;

modern.text: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit,

original.text: אִם הָלַ֥כְתִּי עִם שָׁ֑וְא וַתַּ֖חַשׁ עַל מִרְמָ֣ה רַגְלִֽי

verses.restored: let him weigh me in scales of justice, and let the Divine know my integrity.

familiar.text: Let me be weighed in an even balance that God may know mine integrity.

modern.text: let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.

original.text: יִשְׁקְלֵ֥נִי בְמֹאזְנֵי צֶ֑דֶק וְיֵדַ֥ע אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ תֻּמָּתִֽי

verses.restored: If my step has turned from the way, and my heart walked after my eyes, and any stain has clung to my palms,

familiar.text: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;

modern.text: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands,

original.text: אִ֥ם תִּטֶּ֣ה אַשֻּׁרִי֮ מִנִּ֪י הַ֫דָּ֥רֶךְ וְאַחַ֣ר עֵ֭ינַי הָלַ֣ךְ לִבִּ֑י וּ֝בְכַפַּ֗י דָּ֣בַק מֻאֽוּם

verses.restored: then let me sow and another eat, and let what grows for me be rooted out.

familiar.text: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.

modern.text: then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.

original.text: אֶ֭זְרְעָה וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל וְֽצֶאֱצָאַ֥י יְשֹׁרָֽשׁוּ

verses.restored: If my heart has been enticed toward a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbor’s doorway,

familiar.text: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door;

modern.text: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door,

original.text: אִם נִפְתָּ֣ה לִ֭בִּי עַל אִשָּׁ֑ה וְעַל פֶּ֖תַח רֵעִ֣י אָרָֽבְתִּי

verses.restored: then let my woman grind for another, and let others bow over her.

familiar.text: Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.

modern.text: then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.

original.text: תִּטְחַ֣ן לְאַחֵ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝עָלֶ֗יהָ יִכְרְע֥וּן אֲחֵרִֽין

verses.restored: For that would be a shameful act, and it would be an iniquity for judges.

familiar.text: For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.

modern.text: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.

original.text: כִּי הוא זִמָּ֑ה והיא עָוֺ֥ן פְּלִילִֽים

verses.restored: For it is a fire that consumes to Abaddon and would root out all my increase.

familiar.text: For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.

modern.text: For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.

original.text: כִּ֤י אֵ֣שׁ הִ֭יא עַד אֲבַדּ֣וֹן תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּֽבְכָל תְּב֖וּאָתִ֣י תְשָׁרֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: If I rejected the case of my male servant or my female servant when they contended with me,

familiar.text: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;

modern.text: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me,

original.text: אִם אֶמְאַ֗ס מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַ֭בְדִּי וַאֲמָתִ֑י בְּ֝רִבָ֗ם עִמָּדִֽי

verses.restored: what then would I do when the Divine rises? When he visits, what would I answer him?

familiar.text: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

modern.text: what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?

original.text: וּמָ֣ה אֶֽ֭עֱשֶׂה כִּֽי יָק֣וּם אֵ֑ל וְכִֽי יִ֝פְקֹ֗ד מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: Did not the One who made me in the womb make him? Did not one form us in the womb?

familiar.text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?

modern.text: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?

original.text: הֲֽ֝לֹא בַ֭בֶּטֶן עֹשֵׂ֣נִי עָשָׂ֑הוּ וַ֝יְכֻנֶ֗נּוּ בָּרֶ֥חֶם אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: If I withheld the desire of the poor, or caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

familiar.text: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

modern.text: If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,

original.text: אִם אֶ֭מְנַע מֵחֵ֣פֶץ דַּלִּ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י אַלְמָנָ֣ה אֲכַלֶּֽה

verses.restored: or ate my morsel alone, and the orphan did not eat from it,

familiar.text: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;

modern.text: if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless—

original.text: וְאֹכַ֣ל פִּתִּ֣י לְבַדִּ֑י וְלֹא אָכַ֖ל יָת֣וֹם מִמֶּֽנָּה

verses.restored: for from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided her,

familiar.text: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother’s womb;)

modern.text: though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow—

original.text: כִּ֣י מִ֭נְּעוּרַי גְּדֵלַ֣נִי כְאָ֑ב וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן אִמִּ֣י אַנְחֶֽנָּה

verses.restored: if I saw anyone perishing without clothing, or a needy one without covering,

familiar.text: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;

modern.text: if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak,

original.text: אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֭וֹבֵד מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָאֶבְיֽוֹן

verses.restored: if his loins did not bless me, and he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep,

familiar.text: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

modern.text: if his heart has not blessed me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep,

original.text: אִם לֹ֣א בֵרֲכ֣וּנִי חלצו וּמִגֵּ֥ז כְּ֝בָשַׂי יִתְחַמָּֽם

verses.restored: if I raised my hand against the orphan because I saw my help in the gate,

familiar.text: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:

modern.text: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless because I saw that I had support in the gate,

original.text: אִם הֲנִיפ֣וֹתִי עַל יָת֣וֹם יָדִ֑י כִּֽי אֶרְאֶ֥ה בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר עֶזְרָתִֽי

verses.restored: then let my shoulder fall from its shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from its socket.

familiar.text: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.

modern.text: then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.

original.text: כְּ֭תֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָ֣ה תִפּ֑וֹל וְ֝אֶזְרֹעִ֗י מִקָּנָ֥ה תִשָּׁבֵֽר

verses.restored: For calamity from the Divine was dread to me, and because of his majesty I could not do such things.

familiar.text: For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.

modern.text: For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.

original.text: כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד אֵ֭לַי אֵ֣יד אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִשְּׂאֵת֗וֹ לֹ֣א אוּכָֽל

verses.restored: If I made gold my confidence, or called fine gold my trust,

familiar.text: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;

modern.text: If I have put my trust in gold or called pure gold my security,

original.text: אִם שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י וְ֝לַכֶּ֗תֶם אָמַ֥רְתִּי מִבְטַחִֽי

verses.restored: if I rejoiced because my wealth was great and because my hand had found much,

familiar.text: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;

modern.text: if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much,

original.text: אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י וְכִֽי כַ֝בִּ֗יר מָצְאָ֥ה יָדִֽי

verses.restored: if I saw the light when it shone, or the moon moving in splendor,

familiar.text: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;

modern.text: if I have beheld the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,

original.text: אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ

verses.restored: and my heart was secretly enticed, and my hand kissed my mouth,

familiar.text: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:

modern.text: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,

original.text: וַיִּ֣פְתְּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לִבִּ֑י וַתִּשַּׁ֖ק יָדִ֣י לְפִֽי

verses.restored: this also would be an iniquity for judges, for I would have denied the Divine above.

familiar.text: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.

modern.text: this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.

original.text: גַּם ה֭וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י כִּֽי כִחַ֖שְׁתִּי לָאֵ֣ל מִמָּֽעַל

verses.restored: If I rejoiced at the ruin of one who hated me, or exulted when evil found him,

familiar.text: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:

modern.text: If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him—

original.text: אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י וְ֝הִתְעֹרַ֗רְתִּי כִּֽי מְצָ֥אוֹ רָֽע

verses.restored: I did not allow my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse.

familiar.text: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.

modern.text: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse—

original.text: וְלֹא נָתַ֣תִּי לַחֲטֹ֣א חִכִּ֑י לִשְׁאֹ֖ל בְּאָלָ֣ה נַפְשֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: If the people of my tent did not say, Who can find one not filled with his meat?

familiar.text: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.

modern.text: if the men of my house have not said, ‘Who is there who has not had his fill?’—

original.text: אִם לֹ֣א אָ֭מְרוּ מְתֵ֣י אָהֳלִ֑י מִֽי יִתֵּ֥ן מִ֝בְּשָׂר֗וֹ לֹ֣א נִשְׂבָּֽע

verses.restored: The sojourner did not lodge outside; I opened my doors to the wayfarer.

familiar.text: The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.

modern.text: but no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler—

original.text: בַּ֭חוּץ לֹא יָלִ֣ין גֵּ֑ר דְּ֝לָתַ֗י לָאֹ֥רַח אֶפְתָּֽח

verses.restored: If I covered my transgressions like Adam/humanity, hiding my guilt in my bosom,

familiar.text: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:

modern.text: if I have covered my transgressions like Adam by hiding my guilt in my heart,

original.text: אִם כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י לִטְמ֖וֹן בְּחֻבִּ֣י עֲוֺֽנִי

verses.restored: because I feared the great multitude, or the contempt of clans terrified me, so that I kept silence and did not go out of the door,

familiar.text: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door?

modern.text: because I greatly feared the crowds and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and would not go outside—

original.text: כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱר֨וֹץ הָ֘מ֤וֹן רַבָּ֗ה וּבוּז מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת יְחִתֵּ֑נִי וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם לֹא אֵ֥צֵא פָֽתַח

verses.restored: Oh, that I had one to hear me! Look, my mark/signature. Let Shaddai answer me, and let my accuser write a document.

familiar.text: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book.

modern.text: (Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser compose an indictment.

original.text: מִ֤י יִתֶּן לִ֨י שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ לִ֗י הֶן תָּ֭וִי שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְסֵ֥פֶר כָּ֝תַ֗ב אִ֣ישׁ רִיבִֽי

verses.restored: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it on me like a crown.

familiar.text: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.

modern.text: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.

original.text: אִם לֹ֣א עַל שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ אֶֽעֶנְדֶ֖נּוּ עֲטָר֣וֹת לִֽי

verses.restored: I would declare to him the number of my steps; like a prince I would approach him.

familiar.text: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.

modern.text: I would give account of all my steps; I would approach Him like a prince.)—

original.text: מִסְפַּ֣ר צְ֭עָדַי אַגִּידֶ֑נּוּ כְּמוֹ נָ֝גִ֗יד אֲקָרֲבֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: If my ground cries out against me, and its furrows weep together,

familiar.text: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;

modern.text: if my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,

original.text: אִם עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק וְ֝יַ֗חַד תְּלָמֶ֥יהָ יִבְכָּיֽוּן

verses.restored: if I have eaten its strength without silver, or caused the soul of its owners to breathe out,

familiar.text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:

modern.text: if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,

original.text: אִם כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי כָ֑סֶף וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלֶ֣יהָ הִפָּֽחְתִּי

verses.restored: let thorns grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

familiar.text: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

modern.text: then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Thus conclude the words of Job.

original.text: תַּ֤חַת חִטָּ֨ה יֵ֥צֵא ח֗וֹחַ וְתַֽחַת שְׂעֹרָ֥ה בָאְשָׁ֑ה תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב
